title: Modified Drop Tower Impact Tests for American Football Helmets
protocol: Construct NOCSAE twin-wire drop carriage assembly as defined in NOCSAE DOC.001.
Verify that all components of the assembly are securely attached.
Align the headform collar with the desired position on the headform rotator adjuster.
Tighten the headform threaded lock ring to attach the size "large" NOCSAE headform.
Refer to Section 5 of NOCSAE DOC.100 for new or repaired headforms.
Securely attach the triaxial accelerometer to the accelerometer plate located at the center of gravity of the headform.
Place the accelerometer in the center of the accelerometer plate, lining up both holes with the holes in the plate.
Insert and tighten two screws using an Allen head screwdriver until securely mounted.
Configure the data acquisition system according to manufacturer's specifications.
Connect the cables for the data acquisition assembly.
Connect the accelerometer cable to the three-way coaxial splitter.
Attach a coaxial cable from each output of the coaxial splitter to sensor input ports on the amplifier module (channels 1, 2, and 3).
Connect coaxial cables from the output ports of the amplifier module (channels 1, 2, and 3) to the front of the data acquisition system.
Attach one end of the RS-232 cable to the rear connector of the data acquisition system.
Connect the other end of the RS-232 cable to Com Port 1 on the Personal Computer (PC).
Power on the PC and log in.
Download and install the data acquisition system software onto the computer.
Power on the data acquisition assembly.
Plug in each component's 120 volt outlet into a power source.
Flip the amplifier toggle switch to the "on" position.
Double-click the data acquisition program icon located on the desktop to open the software.
Click "yes" when prompted to check module status.
Load the Test Setup File.
Click the "Setup" tab, scroll down to "Open", and then select "Test Setup".
Browse the computer directory, locate, and select the test setup file labeled "NOCSAE1.TSF".
Click "Load".
Enter sensor information for the accelerometers.
Click the yellow Sensor Input icon for channel 3 in the active Module.
Insert the calibration value (mV/G) for the z-axis accelerometer into the "CAL Value" text box.
Click the "PREV" button.
Repeat steps for the y-axis accelerometer (channel 2).
Repeat steps for the x-axis accelerometer (channel 1).
Click the green "Return" icon to exit sensor.
Click the green "Save" icon and then name the Test Setup as "NOCSAE-JoVE".
Click "save".
Select the helmet model for impact testing.
For helmet certification, select samples according to NOCSAE DOC.011.24.
Test the sample according to Table 1 and Figures 1 and 2.
Select corresponding faceguards for each selected helmet model.
Conduct base helmet impact tests with the baseline faceguard for such helmet.
Adjust headform and anvil to the desired impact orientation using the headform rotator assembly and anvil guide rail.
Remove the taper-loc bolt from the headform rotator assembly and orient the headform adjuster to align bolt-holes to the desired position.
Insert and securely fasten the taper-loc bolt.
Loosen the headform threaded lock ring and rotate the headform nose position to the required orientation.
Securely tighten the headform threaded lock ring.
Loosen the two base plate-anvil bolts and slide anvil until the desired impact location is achieved.
Tighten base plate-anvil bolts and ensure all connections are securely fastened.
Attach release system to drop carriage assembly.
Lift the drop carriage assembly to the height of the release system.
Center the release system to its attachment point on the drop carriage assembly.
Flip the toggle switch for the electromagnetic release system to the "On" position.
Raise drop carriage assembly to the specific height determined to achieve the desired impact velocity.
Load the Test Setup File in the data acquisition system.
Click the "Test" tab, and then click "Collect Data".
Browse the computer directory, locate and select the test setup file labeled "NOCSAE-JoVE.TSF".
Click "Load".
Click "OK".
Type a test description in the "Description" dialog box and then press the "Tab" key.
Provide a 5 character test ID, Type "JoVE1" and click "Continue".
Click "Continue".
Observe the instrumentation warming up.
Once the counter has reached 15 s, click "Continue".
Observe the system automatically performing accelerometer calibration.
Once all boxes are colored green, click "continue".

Using the release system, drop the carriage assembly and trigger the data acquisition system to record the event by simultaneously flipping both toggle switches located on the release system power control box.
Calculate and record the resulting SI value.
Ensure the result is 1,200 SI ±2%.
Repeat steps for each of the three required impact locations until results are obtained.
Exchange the MEP pad used for calibration for the MEP test pad.
Select impact location and velocity for testing according to Table 1.
Impacts must be conducted from lowest drop velocity to the highest.
Ambient temperature impacts should be conducted before conditioned impacts.
Adjust the headform orientation and anvil position to achieve the desired impact location.
Select the helmet for testing.
Fit the selected helmet to the headform according to the manufacturer's instructions and NOCSAE procedures.
Securely attach the helmet's chinstrap to the headform.
Apply talcum powder lightly if necessary due to faceguard constraints.
Attach the mechanical release system to the drop carriage assembly.
Raise the drop carriage assembly to the specific height for the desired impact velocity.
Ready the data acquisition system for recording an event.
Drop the carriage assembly using the mechanical release system and trigger the data acquisition system simultaneously.
Record SI, HIC, and peak acceleration results immediately after impact.
Compare recorded results with pass/fail criteria.
Set a pass/fail value of 700 SI for impacts at speeds of 5.46 m/sec, 4.88 m/sec, and 4.23 m/sec.
Maintain the pass/fail criterion of 300 SI for impacts at 3.46 m/sec.
Repeat steps until results are obtained for all required impacts.
Perform a system check upon completion of testing.
Maintain results.
Compare pre-test and post-test system checks.
Ensure that any variation is 7% or less.
